correctness.rationale: The projector onto the power-sketch columns Y=[kappa^{2q+1}g;H] has P_11=kappa^{4q+2}gamma/(1+kappa^{4q+2}gamma), gamma=g(H^TH)^{-1}g^T. Orthogonal regression identifies gamma distributed as chi²_k/chi²_{d-k}, independent, for all 1<=k<d. The Frobenius trace identity yields the full excess distribution and beta integral; Euler integration produces hypergeometric expectation. For fixed dimension and k, t→∞ beta endpoint dominated convergence gives t^{-1/2} for k=1, (log t)/t for k=2 and t^{-1} times (d-k)/(k-2) for k>=3. Multiplying by kappa²-1 gives all coefficients, including d=2,k=1 and kappa=1. Independent numerical QR/chi-square beta integral checks corroborate; fixed d,k,q essential.

evidence: Existing large matrix/randomized subspace power bounds consider general spectra and tail ranks, but do not give equality in distribution of the one-spike projector error for every k and arbitrary fixed power q.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The broader spectral families are not stronger *exact-distribution* theorems: bound coverage does not imply the chi-square mixture or its sharp coefficients. Nonetheless a general Wishart projection identity could imply part of the result, so it remains a residual risk.

value.rationale: The Gaussian range finder is fundamental; its zero-oversampling small-sketch moments have a genuine finite-moment cutoff k=2 exactly where a reciprocal chi-square expectation changes integrability. Exact risk and power-count coefficients inform algorithm behavior on a natural spectral stress test and can be reused in benchmark analyses, not merely a tiny numerical example.

limitations: Only real symmetric one-spike matrices, exact arithmetic, fixed d,k,q, squared Frobenius excess; no high-dimensional joint limit.
Wishart specialty literature might already contain equivalent exact beta statements.
